ticker_news.title: 3 Stocks I'd Rather Own Than Apple With a CEO Shakeup
ticker_news.description: With Tim Cook stepping down as Apple CEO in September 2026 and John Ternus taking over, the article argues that leadership transitions create uncertainty. Apple trades at a premium valuation (34x earnings) without strong growth prospects and lacks a clear AI strategy. The author recommends Nvidia, Microsoft, and Alphabet as better investment alternatives due to their strong AI exposure, cloud computing growth, and more attractive valuations.
ticker_news.author: Keithen Drury

ticker_news.title: Apple Posts Double Beat In Q2 As Active Installed Base Hits All-Time High — 'Our Best March Quarter Ever'
ticker_news.description: Apple reported fiscal Q2 2026 revenue of $111.18 billion and EPS of $2.01, both beating analyst estimates. Revenue grew 17% YoY and EPS climbed 22% YoY, driven by strong iPhone 17 demand and record March quarter performance. The company's active installed base hit all-time highs across all product categories. Apple authorized an additional $100 billion share repurchase program and increased its quarterly dividend by 4%. Despite the strong earnings beat, AAPL stock declined 0.50% in after-hours trading.
ticker_news.author: Adam Eckert

ticker_news.title: Stock Market Today, April 30: U.S. Markets Surge Higher Despite a Mixed Bag of Earnings From Big Tech
ticker_news.description: U.S. markets rose on April 30, 2026, with the S&P 500 gaining 1.02%, Nasdaq up 0.89%, and Dow jumping 1.62%. Alphabet surged 10% on strong earnings and AI commentary, while Microsoft and Meta declined 4% and 9% respectively due to concerns over massive AI capital expenditure. Caterpillar also rallied 10% on robust results, helping fuel the Dow's gains.
ticker_news.author: Josh Kohn-Lindquist

ticker_news.title: Apple Stock Pops On Strong Q3 Guidance: Details
ticker_news.description: Apple delivered a strong fiscal Q2 earnings beat with $111.18B in revenue (up 17% YoY) and $2.01 EPS, exceeding expectations. The company guided for June-quarter revenue growth of 14-17%, well ahead of Street expectations of ~9%. Apple also announced a 4% dividend increase, $100B in share repurchases, and signaled a shift away from its net cash-neutral balance sheet strategy. The stock rose 3.59% in after-hours trading.
ticker_news.author: Erica Kollmann

ticker_news.title: While "Magnificent Seven" Companies Pour Hundreds of Billions into AI Infrastructure, Apple Continues to Execute the Classic Shareholder-Friendly Playbook
ticker_news.description: Apple reported Q2 2026 earnings that beat estimates, raising its quarterly dividend by 4% to $0.27 per share and authorizing a $100 billion share repurchase program. While other 'Magnificent Seven' companies like Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta are investing heavily in AI infrastructure with capex exceeding $100 billion annually, Apple continues its traditional shareholder-friendly approach, having repurchased $37 billion in stock and distributed $7.7 billion in dividends in the first half of fiscal 2026.
ticker_news.author: Bram Berkowitz

ticker_news.title: 1 Reason Apple Is Still My Favorite Stock I'd Hand Down to My Grandkids
ticker_news.description: Apple is highlighted as a long-term 'forever stock' with exceptional historical returns (20% annualized since 1980, 29% over the past decade). While its walled garden ecosystem has driven dominance, the article argues that Apple's strongest competitive advantage is its brand loyalty—with 96.4% of iPhone users planning to upgrade to another iPhone and a 92% customer retention rate. Even if regulatory pressures weaken its ecosystem, the author believes Apple's brand strength will sustain investor confidence and stock performance for decades.
ticker_news.author: Dave Kovaleski
